name: plan-lanes-4
summary: Optional: one writer and three reviewers, each with an assigned duty (a lane); unanimous sign-off. Experimental.
description: Optional and experimental (0.8.2): one writer and three reviewers, each reviewer carrying a lane, meaning an assigned duty it looks at first: correctness and interfaces (OpenAI GPT-5.6 Luna), security and failure behaviour (Google Gemini 3.8 Flash), implementation and verification (Z.ai GLM 5.3 Flash). A lane is where a reviewer's attention goes first, never a smaller set of criteria: every reviewer still writes a row for every criterion and still flags a serious problem outside its lane. Anthropic Sonnet 5.5 writes the draft, every revision and the handoff and holds no panel seat; Meta Llama 4 Maverick writes the criteria. No blind proposals and no debate: one writer, three independent reviews, unanimous sign-off, a round cap of 7 and the same stall rule as the other planning chains. The roster is a starting hypothesis, not a measured optimum, and nothing here claims it plans better than another chain: it cannot be measured without ground truth. STATE: the words that tell each reviewer its lane are recorded in src/roles.js (LANE_TEXT) with the 0.8.2 prompt re-record; they have been read only by mock seats, no real seat has run this chain. GLM 5.3 Flash's panel review is allowed 360,000 output tokens (panelMaxTokens): of the OpenRouter endpoints that are zero-data-retention, only some accept that many completion tokens (8 of 17 inside the price cap on 2026-10-06 for the add-on seat; this chain does not set a price cap), and whether OpenRouter routes around one that does not, or refuses the call, is not verified. Every seat states reasoning high where its model takes a setting; GLM 5.3 Flash's own default is above high, so it gets none. One OpenRouter key covers every seat.
